12 December 2011 
• 
Gold, silver and platinum traded mainly in response 
to newsflow last week as all eyes focussed on the 
ECB summit. A spectacular crash on Thursday saw 
prices plummet as headlines began to emerge that 
ECB chief Mario Draghi would not countenance 
Eurozone bond purchases. By Friday, all bets were 
off as news that British Prime Minister David Cam-
eron had vetoed a proposed EU treaty change left a 
cloud of doubt surrounding the long-term conse-
quences of the summit.  
 
• 
Palladium followed its own path, however, and was 
the only one of the major precious metals to post 
gains last week. Investors that had begun the week 
short palladium were doubtless driven to cover after 
prices held above $630 on Monday and into Tues-
day. In addition, an accumulation of option interest 
at key levels helped maintain buying above $660.  
 
• 
The SPDR Gold Trust—the largest gold ETF by 
holdings—was a seller last week, shedding more 
than 81,000 ounces. Total gold ETF holdings none-
theless increased for the ninth consecutive week, 
and now exceed 70.4 million ounces. Platinum and 
palladium ETF flows were very subdued, following 
heavy liquidation in the previous week. 
 
• 
Net long speculative gold positions on COMEX in-
creased for the second consecutive week, up more 
than 1.1 million ounces to 22.6 million ounces in 
total. Increases were especially notable in large 
speculative options positions, which rose by more 
than 16%.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
12 December 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
The gold price washed around largely at the 
mercy of newsflow last week as all eyes focussed 
on Thursday’s ECB summit. Yet again, we saw a 
broadly positive correlation with risk sentiment; 
gold has still yet to rediscover the safe-haven ap-
peal that was so instrumental in driving the great 
gains made in the summer. Having begun the 
week above $1,750, gold was sold down almost 
to $1,700 by Tuesday. As optimism increased 
towards the beginning of the summit, gold recov-
ered steadily towards the week’s opening level. A 
spectacular crash on Thursday, however, saw 
prices drop $50 in no time at all as headlines be-
gan to emerge that ECB chief Mario Draghi would 
not countenance Eurozone bond purchases. By 
Friday, all bets were off as news that British 
Prime Minister David Cameron had vetoed a pro-
posed EU treaty change left a cloud of doubt sur-
rounding the long-term consequences of the sum-
mit. Gold traded in a jittery $20 range, with most 
investors reluctant to commit either way given the 
prevailing uncertainty over the Eurozone’s next 
moves. 
 
• 
Net long speculative positions on COMEX in-
creased for the second consecutive week, up 
more than 1.1 million ounces to 22.6 million 
ounces in total. Increases were especially notable 
in large speculative options positions, which rose 
by more than 16%. Liquidation of TOCOM posi-
tions accelerated this week, with declines of 
248,000 ounces dwarfing the previous week’s 
decline of 9,700 ounces. 
 
• 
The SPDR Gold Trust—the largest gold ETF by 
holdings—was a seller last week, shedding more 
than 81,000 ounces. Total gold ETF holdings 
nonetheless increased for the ninth consecutive 
week, and now exceed 70.4 million ounces.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
12 December 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
Silver ETF Investment, Jan 07—December 11 
• 
Silver moved largely in tandem with gold last 
week, vulnerable to the same headline-driven 
moves as the yellow metal. Thursday’s liquidation 
was felt more acutely in silver: with spot having 
been bid as high as $33.24, the subsequent 
sweep down to $31.40 represented a drop of 
nearly 5.9%. From this low, prices recovered on 
Friday to end the week above $32.00—barely a 
dollar lower than where they had started on Mon-
day. 
 
• 
Net long speculative positions in silver increased 
by 8.8 million ounces in the first week of Decem-
ber—a strong rebound in favour of long interest 
after the net shortening that was seen at the end 
of November. This reversal was driven by an im-
pressive increase in small speculative futures 
positions, which alone accounted for more than 
6.4 million ounces of the total increase. Large 
speculative options positions remain healthy, de-
spite a small reduction last week. 
 
• 
Most of the major silver ETFs added to their hold-
ings last week. However, these were more than 
offset by liquidation of more nearly 3.7 million 
ounces from the US ETFS fund. Overall silver 
ETF holdings decreased by 1.4 million ounces; 
following the previous week’s addition of 2.8 mil-
lion ounces, we see that silver ETF flows are as 
prone to fluctuations as the price of the metal it-
self.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
12 December 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
The only way was down for platinum last week as 
nervousness leading up to the EU summit 
weighed heavily on prices. Spot platinum made 
lows around $1,487 on Friday, down from almost 
$1,560 on Monday. A late rally leading to an end-
of-week close at $1,515 could hardly disguise the 
fact that it had been a poor week for platinum. The 
declines continued a downtrend extending back to 
mid-November, and the break below $1,500 at the 
end of the week marked the first breach of this 
level since mid-October.  
 
• 
The platinum futures markets experienced another 
relatively quiet week, with very little to report on 
NYMEX. Liquidation amounting to 50,000 ounces 
on TOCOM was evidence of heightened bearish-
ness towards platinum. 
 
• 
After shedding more than 70,000 ounces in the 
last week of November, platinum ETFs were 
largely inactive last week, their selling energy 
spent for the moment. Relative stasis could persist 
as long as platinum remains between $1,500-
$1,550; expect activity to recommence if we see a 
breakout either side of this zone.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
12 December 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Palladium Exchange Investment, Apr 09—December 11 
Palladium ETF Investment, Apr 07—December 11 
• 
In contrast to the other three major precious met-
als, palladium made solid gains last week, ending 
Friday above $680, up $40 from Monday. Our im-
pression is that speculative players, whose in-
creased involvement in palladium has been nota-
ble of late, were largely responsible for palladium’s 
outperformance. Investors that had begun the 
week short palladium were doubtless driven to 
cover after prices held above $630 on Monday and 
into Tuesday. In addition, an accumulation of op-
tion interest at key levels helped maintain buying 
above $660.  
 
• 
The first week in December saw speculative fu-
tures positions increase by more than 80,000 
ounces. Much of this is likely to have been short 
covering—a development we predicted given that 
the previous week’s shortening was followed by a 
sudden and unexpected price hike.  
 
• 
Palladium ETFs on the whole were net liquidators 
last week, shedding 12,000 ounces of physical 
holdings. This is small compared with the previous 
week’s selling of 54,000 ounces, however—
unsurprising given the week’s positive price action. 
Expect palladium ETFs to turn net buyers this 
week if the spot price continues to outperform the 
other precious metals.
